events.title: SC Trip — Networking Weekend
events.description: Travel to South Carolina. Meet Kim Bowman (SCRIN) to discuss partnership and USDA RBDG relationship. Visit UofSC Office of Innovation and Tech Incubator. Reach out to Rep. Bradley's office to introduce the initiative. Begin building the in-state partner network.

events.title: Reserve Nonprofit Name
events.description: File name reservation with SC Secretary of State at businessfilings.sc.gov. Cost: $10. Reservation holds the name for 120 days while the rest of the formation paperwork is completed. Also purchase the .org domain at the same time.

events.title: Board Member Recruitment Deadline
events.description: Confirm all 3 initial board members by this date. Need full legal names, addresses, and written confirmation of willingness to serve. All board member info must be ready before filing Articles of Incorporation on March 15. Consider SC-based candidates with community ties or technology backgrounds.

events.title: File Articles of Incorporation
events.description: Submit Form NP to the SC Secretary of State online at businessfilings.sc.gov. Cost: $32.50. Include charitable purpose clause with IRS-required language and dissolution clause. Processing takes 1-2 business days. This is the legal birth certificate of the nonprofit.

events.title: Get EIN from IRS
events.description: Apply for Employer Identification Number on IRS.gov. Free and instant — takes about 15 minutes online. Available Monday-Friday 7am-10pm Eastern Time. Screenshot the confirmation immediately. EIN is needed for the bank account, 501(c)(3) application, and every future grant application.

events.title: Draft Bylaws Complete
events.description: Finalize bylaws and conflict of interest policy documents ready for board review and approval at the March 30 organizational meeting. Use the IRS sample conflict of interest policy. Circulate to all board members at least 5 days before the meeting so they can review in advance.

events.title: Organizational Board Meeting
events.description: First official board meeting (Zoom is fine). Agenda: adopt bylaws, elect officers (President, Secretary, Treasurer), adopt conflict of interest policy, authorize opening a nonprofit bank account, set meeting schedule for the year. Record formal meeting minutes with all votes documented. Have all members sign the minutes.

events.title: OpenAI People-First AI Fund — Application Window Opens
events.description: Priority Tier 1 grant. OpenAI Foundation's $9.5M second wave of the People-First AI Fund. Specifically prioritizes rural communities, AI literacy, and small nonprofits with budgets under $10M. Grants are unrestricted. This is the single highest-priority grant application — plan to submit by May 30.

events.title: File 501(c)(3) Form 1023-EZ
events.description: Submit IRS Form 1023-EZ for federal tax-exempt status at pay.gov. Cost: $275. Requires Articles of Incorporation, bylaws, EIN, program description, and 3-year budget projection. Processing time: 2-6 weeks for 1023-EZ. Once approved, you receive the IRS Determination Letter — the most important document in your nonprofit's life.

events.title: Apply for Google for Nonprofits
events.description: Apply for Google for Nonprofits program at google.com/nonprofits. First register with TechSoup (techsoup.org) for verification — takes 2-5 business days. Upon approval: activate free Google Workspace (professional email with your domain) and Google Ad Grants ($10,000/month in free Google search advertising). Also explore Microsoft for Nonprofits and AWS Nonprofits at the same time.

events.title: Website & Social Media Launch
events.description: Launch the organization's public-facing website, LinkedIn page, and Facebook page. Website must include mission statement, board bios, program description, contact info, and donation option. This is required before Google Ad Grants can be activated. Grant program officers will Google the organization — this needs to be live and professional before submitting any major applications.

events.title: USDA Rural Development Grant Window Opens
events.description: USDA Rural Business Development Grant (RBDG) application window. Grants of $10K-$500K for rural workforce and economic development. Key advantage: SCRIN is an existing USDA grantee — ask Kim Bowman for a letter of support and guidance on the SC USDA state office relationship before applying. Contact SC USDA Rural Development office in Columbia.

events.title: First Grant Application Submitted
events.description: Submit the first major grant application to the OpenAI People-First AI Fund. Prepare narrative, budget, and supporting documents. Have a board member review before submission. This is a major milestone — the first step in building a track record as an active grant-seeking organization.

events.title: Pilot Workshop Planning Complete
events.description: Complete all planning for the first AI literacy workshop pilot: venue confirmed, curriculum finalized, participant recruitment done, materials printed, facilitator(s) confirmed, logistics in place. The workshop must be ready to run on June 30. Start documenting everything for grant impact reports.

events.title: First AI Literacy Workshop — Pilot
events.description: Host the inaugural AI literacy workshop in a rural South Carolina community. This pilot validates the program model, generates real impact data for grant applications (participant count, demographics, pre/post knowledge assessments, testimonials), and begins building credibility in the community. Photograph everything. Collect feedback forms from every participant.

events.title: Summer Workshop Series
events.description: Run the summer workshop series — target 3-5 additional workshops across different rural SC communities during July and August. Vary locations to demonstrate regional reach. Document all workshops with photos, attendance numbers, and feedback. This data will be essential for fall grant applications. Partner with local libraries and community centers as hosts.

events.title: Microsoft/OpenAI Societal Resilience Fund Deadline
events.description: Application deadline for the Microsoft and OpenAI Societal Resilience Fund ($2M fund). By this point you should have completed at least 1-2 workshops with documented outcomes. Use workshop impact data — participant numbers, demographics, testimonials — to strengthen the application narrative about serving vulnerable communities.

events.title: Expected 501(c)(3) Determination Received
events.description: Expected date to receive the IRS 501(c)(3) Determination Letter (filed April 15, approximately 3-6 months processing). This letter is the golden key that unlocks: Google for Nonprofits full activation, SC state tax exemption, charitable solicitation registration, most major foundation grants, and corporate sponsorship conversations. Scan and store in multiple secure locations immediately upon receipt.

events.title: Start Incubator Curriculum Design
events.description: Begin designing the innovation incubator program structure: curriculum outline, mentor network recruitment, application process design, cohort selection criteria, graduation requirements, and budget. Research best practices from rural incubators (Appalachian Funders Network, Runway, Opportunity Alabama). Target: incubator design finalized by January 2027.

events.title: NSF Broadening Participation in Computing — Application Deadline
events.description: NSF BPC grant application deadline. Requires 501(c)(3) status (received in September), evidence-based program approach, evaluation plan, and strong partnership with an academic institution. Pursue UofSC partnership before submitting — NSF strongly prefers university collaborators. This is a Tier 2 grant but prestigious and renewable. Grants of $50K-$300K.

events.title: USDA Rural Business Development Grant — Application Deadline
events.description: USDA Rural Business Development Grant final application deadline. By now you have workshop impact data and 501(c)(3) status. Get a letter of support from Kim Bowman at SCRIN before submitting — their existing USDA relationship is a major advantage. Contact the SC USDA Rural Development state office in Columbia to introduce yourself before the final submission.

events.title: End of Year Fundraising Push
events.description: Launch end-of-year individual donor fundraising campaign. December 31 is the biggest giving day of the year for nonprofits — donors want tax deductions before year-end. Prepare an email campaign, social media posts, and a giving page on your website. Share workshop impact stories and photos. Set a modest but achievable fundraising goal (e.g., $5,000 from individual donors).

events.title: First Major Grant Awarded — Target
events.description: Target date to receive the first major grant award — ideally the OpenAI People-First AI Fund (submitted May 30, expected decision by year-end) or the Microsoft/OpenAI Societal Resilience Fund. This milestone validates the fundraising strategy, funds operations through Phase 2 planning, and dramatically increases credibility for all future grant applications.

events.title: First Incubator Cohort Launch
events.description: Launch the inaugural cohort of the Rural AI Innovation Incubator. Target: 8-12 rural South Carolina entrepreneurs building AI-powered businesses. Provide weekly programming, mentor sessions, access to AI tools, business development workshops, and connections to the SC innovation ecosystem (VentureSouth, Nexus SC, SCRA). Cohort runs January through April.

events.title: EDA Tech Hub Grant Application Window
events.description: EDA Tech Hub sub-grant opportunity through SC Nexus. South Carolina is a federally designated Tech Hub — SC Nexus distributes sub-grants to aligned organizations for workforce development and technology adoption. AI literacy for rural communities is a direct fit. Build the SC Nexus relationship during the SC trip and throughout 2026 before submitting.

events.title: First Incubator Demo Day
events.description: Host the inaugural incubator Demo Day — a public showcase where cohort founders present their AI startups to investors, press, partners, and community members. Invite VentureSouth, UCAN, Palmetto Angel Fund, and corporate sponsors. This event generates earned media, builds funder relationships, and demonstrates the full pipeline from literacy to entrepreneurship.

events.title: Grant Applications Round 2 — Tier 2 Push
events.description: Submit Tier 2 grant applications with the enhanced credibility of completed workshops, 501(c)(3) status, and the incubator launch: NSF BPC renewal, EDA Tech Hub via SC Nexus, and SC Commission for Minority Affairs. Also approach Google.org/aiEDU if not yet funded. Each application should leverage the growing body of impact evidence from Phase 1.

events.title: Corporate Sponsorship Outreach Begins
events.description: Begin formal corporate sponsorship outreach to Google, Microsoft, Amazon Web Services, and Meta. By this point you have 501(c)(3) status, completed workshops, an active incubator, and compelling impact data. Each corporation has CSR budgets for AI education and digital equity. Prepare a professional sponsorship deck with different tiers ($5K, $10K, $25K) and corresponding recognition benefits.

events.title: Fee-for-Service Curriculum Sales Begin
events.description: Approach school districts for the 2027-2028 school year Title I spending plans. Libraries and community colleges are also strong targets. By September 2027 you have a proven curriculum with documented outcomes — now it is a product you can sell. Target $500-$2,500 per workshop session. This earned revenue diversifies funding and builds long-term sustainability.

events.title: Investment Fund Research Begins
events.description: Begin researching legal structures and models for a rural AI investment fund. Engage a financial attorney and CPA to explore options: CDFI (Community Development Financial Institution), donor-advised fund, LLC/LP structure, or a program-related investment (PRI) vehicle. Study successful models: Runway, Opportunity Alabama, and rural CDFI funds. Target: fund structure decided by June 2028.

events.title: Fund Structure Established
events.description: Legal structure for the investment fund established. All legal and financial advisory work complete. Fund thesis documented. Initial capital commitments secured from lead investors. Deal flow pipeline identified from incubator alumni. Fund ready to make its first investment.

events.title: First Investment Made
events.description: Deploy the first capital investment into a rural South Carolina AI startup — ideally an alumnus of the incubator program. This completes the full flywheel: AI literacy education → business incubation → capital investment → economic impact. A landmark moment for SCAiL and for rural South Carolina.
